newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares up in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares up in lacklustre trade.

text.p: Trading was dull on the Nigerian stock market on Tuesday, dampened by poor corporate results and investors' lack of interest, dealers said.
But the all-share index rose to 8517.46 from 5514.97 on Monday on the back of gains in food company shares amid few price movements.

Traders said the market was bogged down by disappointing company results showing lower profits and shortage of money in the market. Tuesday's result announcement by Mobil Nigeria Plc showed no departure from the pattern already established by other petroleum marketers.
The company said its after-tax profit to end-1996 fell to 933.7 million naira from 1.2 billion naira a year earlier.
Analysts said Mobil performed better than most of its competitiors.
"This one was a lot better when compared to a drop of about 80 percent in the after-tax profit announced by National Oil and Chemical Marketing Co recently," one said.
Oil shares were unchanged on Tuesday as did most other blue chips caught in recent weakening prices.
Adjustment for dividend saw conglomerate A.G. Leventis drop eight kobo to 2.39 naira while oil miller P.S. Mandrides lost 35 kobo to 5.90 naira for the same reason.
Consistent gainers Nestle ended 20 kobo stronger at 48.70 naira and Flour Mills was 15 kobo better at 18.10 naira.
Insurer Crusader joined gainers albeit moderately, notching one kobo to end at 3.18 naira.
